Worth noting for consolers out there. Pass through is limited to 4k60. Need to step up to the flagship for 120hz. (or just.. Console straight into TV etc).
[ozbozb123] My TCL C8K has two 120hz ports. So to have both my XSX and PS5 running at 120, I would need the flagship and connect one of the consoles to the soundbar and the other to port 2? If so, would the audio for port 2 still come out of the soundbar?
Eg would this work to still get 120hz
Soundbar into HDMI1 (120hz) for eARC, PS5 plugged into the soundbar
XSX plugged into HDMI2 (120hz)
Switch 2 plugged into HDMI3 (60hz)
Firestick plugged into HDMI4 (60hz)
[ReaperX22] With the 990H you mean?
It has two hdmi in on the soundbar. You'd plug both the ps5 and the xsx into the soundbar. Soundbar earc into the earc port on the TV. Must be the specific earc port, there's usually only one. Otherwise your setup also works just fine using hdmi2 for xsx. The only real benefit is if you want that other 120hz port(TV) for something else, the soundbar acts as a hdmi switch basically between your consoles. The other benefit is specific audio format support sometimes not available via the TV direct but can bypass it entirely by using the hdmi ports on the soundbar if preferred.
Switch and firestick just straight into TV as normal.
But yes you'd need the flagship if you wanted to run 120hz pass through.

[ReaperX22] Better is subjective in this sense.
Used home theatre gear will always win on positioning and in most cases musicality as well. Soundbars serve a different purpose imo. They're cleaner. Easier to setup. Don't require that bulky receiver and a bajillion wires. They'll often have more 'features' (smart features built in steaming etc) over older home theatre setup.
If you JUST want the best bang for buck audio wise, the home theatre set ups will win almost everytime, but you have to be willing to put in a bit of setup effort usually plus all the wires involved.
I can see the appeal of soundbar simplicity but personally I run a simple 2.0 Edifier s3000 pros for our TV via optical, which also has xlr in from our cd player + line in from our chrome cast audio, bypassing those other streaming requirement options.. And sounding infinitely better for music though loses out in movies.
Imo, the best halfway point is a decent receiver that is 'good enough', and a 3.1 speaker setup. It's great for music, great for dialogue in shows and movies, and doesn't require the rear setup hassle, mess, extra wires away from the TV unit.
Sound is subjective though and so are required features so… Ymmv.

[S Baldrick] I have a TCL TV (C845) with a Samsung soundbar (Q930C), and have had audio latency issues (DTS HD and Dolby TrueHD requiring a +150ms offset) with my 4K Blu-ray Player, and get the TV re-enabling the internal speakers every 15-20 minutes with my Chromecast.
The audio latency problem was there from the beginning (eARC enabled, plugging directly into the soundbar Vs the TV made no difference), but the speaker problem happened after a buggy soundbar firmware update. Even with automatic updates disabled via the SmartThings app, it STILL gets updates - the most recent major bug being the soundbar randomly muting when turning on my TV, requiring a TV reboot.
I'm happy with the sound quality, but the buggy updates make me hesitant to recommend a Samsung soundbar.
